newsitem.title: JAPAN: G7 made no request on Japan fiscal reform -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: G7 made no request on Japan fiscal reform -- MOF.

text.p: The Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations made no specific request at their meeting on Sunday regarding Japan's plan to reform its fiscal balance, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.
"They made no conditions at all regarding Japan's fiscal reform schedule," Mitsuzuka said.
He added that Japan explained at the meeting the schedule and progress of its fiscal reform plan, and asked for G7 support.

On the communique issued at the end of the meeting in Washington, Mitsuzuka, speaking shortly after his return to Japan, said markets may not have expected the G7 members to so strongly express their will on currencies through the joint statement.
"I think it will take some time for the market to fully absorb the real intention" of the statement, he said.
He read out an extract from the communique in which the G7 emphasised the importance of avoiding exchange rates that could lead to the reemergence of large external imbalances.

On Japan's reform of its fiscal balance, the United States has expressed concern about Japan's strong drive to put its house in order regarding its budget. Washington is concerned that such a commitment could be a drag on the Japanese economy, and has asked Japan to moderate the speed of its budget reform schedule.
